beat.title: 2 · Dead horses and ambush
beat.tv: Show The empty horses first. After goblins are seen or attack, use Road ambush · revealed; switch to the gridded road map when positions matter.
read: The trail bends between close woods. Two horses lie across the road ahead, dead and pierced by black-feathered arrows. Their saddlebags hang open. Neither rider is in sight.

The open saddlebags and arrows give you more to examine than the bodies alone. Beyond the bend, trunks and tangled growth break up the view into the woods; anyone moving closer will have to choose where to stand and what to watch.
ask: “What do you do?” Wait for their approach before announcing combat.
On close inspection, identify the horses as Gundren’s and Sildar’s; the saddlebags were looted.
run: Four goblins hide in the woods, two on each side. Roll one goblin Stealth check at +6 and compare it with each traveler’s passive Perception for surprise.
On their first turn, two goblins rush forward while two shoot from cover. Goblins can Hide or Disengage as a bonus action. If three fall, the last tries to flee toward the hideout.
Goblin: AC 15, HP 7, speed 30 ft.; scimitar or shortbow +4 to hit, 1d6+2 damage. Passive Perception 9.
All five player characters choose their own opening actions. Track initiative, cover, and who is actually visible to the goblins.
choices: Let them pick targets, use cover, capture a goblin, pursue a runner, or secure the wagon.
If combat is easy, let it be a clean win. The real problem is finding the missing travelers.
private: Do not show goblin positions on the TV until spotted or until they attack. Stage them on your map with “On TV” unchecked if useful.
